en.headline: Authorities backtrack on mandatory fire escape hoods for hotels
en.dek: The Home Affairs Department will only encourage hotels and guest houses to provide sufficient smoke hoods in rooms, after industry concerns were raised following an earlier statement that they would be required.
body: The Home Affairs Department said on Thursday evening that it would only encourage hotels and guest houses to supply enough smoke hoods in guest rooms to cover maximum occupancy, rather than making the provision mandatory.

The change follows concerns expressed by hotel industry representatives after Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak Mei-kuen indicated earlier that licensed operators would be required to provide fire escape hoods in rooms, staff areas and communal spaces. The department and the Fire Services Department subsequently met the sector.

Under the revised position, no advice will be issued on supply in common or staff areas. The Fire Services Department will provide guidance on how to procure suitable hoods. The department said visitor safety remains paramount and that providing smoke hoods enhances fire safety in an international tourism destination.

zh.headline: 當局改為鼓勵酒店提供逃生頭套 不再強制規定
zh.dek: 民政事務總署回應業界關注後表示，只會鼓勵酒店及賓館在客房按最高住客量提供足夠煙霧頭套，不再強制要求。
body: 民政事務總署星期四晚表示，將只會鼓勵酒店及賓館在客房按最高住客量提供足夠煙霧頭套，而非強制規定必須設置。
早前民政及青年事務局局長麥美娟曾表明持牌經營者須在客房、員工區域及公用地方提供防火逃生頭套，業界其後提出關注，部門與消防處其後與業界會面。
在修訂後的立場下，當局不會就公用地方或員工區域的供應發出建議，消防處則會就如何採購合適頭套提供指引。署方強調保障旅客安全至關重要，提供煙霧頭套有助提升作為國際旅遊城市的消防安全。
